ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows the structural formula of saccharin: on the left is a benzene ring part containing 6 carbons, and on the right is connected a ring structure containing a carbonyl C=O, one N-H, one S atom, and two S=O oxygen atoms. Counting according to the structure in the figure, each molecule of saccharin contains 7 C, 5 H, 3 O, 1 S, and 1 N, so the molecular formula is C7H5NO3S. Reasoning: The available numbers of atoms given by the problem are 30 C, 25 H, 12 O, 8 S, and 14 N. Preparing 1 molecule of saccharin requires C7H5NO3S, so the maximum numbers of molecules that each element can support are respectively: C: floor(30/7)=4; H: floor(25/5)=5; O: floor(12/3)=4; S: floor(8/1)=8; N: floor(14/1)=14. The number of complete molecules that can be formed is determined by the smallest limiting value, therefore at most 4 saccharin molecules can be prepared.
